summary: Intermittent prefetch race in KV prefix layer causing high p99 latency and timeouts for repeat prompts
description: Issue summary: Multiple customer requests (VirtuDocs) observed ~5-15% of repeated prompt requests hitting long tails (p99 > 6s, some 30s timeouts) when sending identical conversation prefixes. Impact: Customer facing increased latency on repeat user prompts causing timeouts and degraded UX during peak hours. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, serving-runtime v1.14.2 with kvcache async-prefetch enabled. Observed behavior: repeat prompts that previously returned <300ms now occasionally take multiple seconds or time out (30s). Expected behavior: cached prefixes should result in sub-500ms latencies for short contexts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a repeat prompt sequence: send prompt A, then follow-up identical prompt A after short interval (5-15s)
2) Repeat at moderate concurrency (10-30 qps) against dedicated endpoint in us-east-1
3) Observe latency distribution on the Redwood API (token-level breakdown).

investigation_notes: 03/09 16:00 - Support: Received VirtuDocs report, escalated to SRE with p99 histograms and example request ids.
03/09 16:20 - SRE: Confirmed spike in p99 for prefix-heavy traffic pattern on dedicated pool; correlation with async-prefetch flip on 2026-02-28 deploy.
03/09 17:10 - Eng (runtime): Reproduced locally by simulating concurrent repeat prompts; saw duplicate origin fetches and lock timeout on kvcache prefetch pipeline.

Hypothesis: The async-prefetch coordinator introduced in v1.14.0 does not correctly deduplicate in-flight prefetches when shard-mapping is rebalanced concurrently, leading to double origin fetches and delayed cache population. This increases per-request latency and occasionally triggers upstream timeouts under load.

Tests performed: A/B test with async-prefetch disabled returned p99 back to baseline; injected artificial shard rebalances to reproduce duplication; added extra instrumentation to measure outstanding prefetches per key.
root_cause: A race condition in the async prefetch coordinator of the kvcache introduced by the shard remapping optimization (v1.14.0). When shard mappings change mid-prefetch, the deduplication key used by the coordinator could differ, causing two concurrent origin fetches for the same logical prefix. The duplicate fetches increased origin load and delayed the first successful cache population, causing p99 latency spikes and occasional 30s upstream timeouts.
resolution_notes: Mitigation (hotfix): Disabled async-prefetch on the affected dedicated pool and reverted the shard-key normalization change via rollback in config (rolled 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC).
Immediate workaround for customer: Enabled synchronous prefix retrieval (config toggle) for VirtuDocs dedicated endpoint; this eliminated the race and brought p99 down to baseline within 15 minutes.

Permanent fix: Engineering created PR #7642 to make deduplication use a stable logical prefix id that survives remapping and added additional unit/integration tests. PR merged to main and scheduled for v1.14.3 rollout (2026-03-12).
Follow-up actions: Add dashboards for outstanding prefetch counts, add alert when duplicate origin fetch rate > 1% for >5m, and add a canary to exercise shard-remap scenarios before global rollouts.
